text:
Kevin Lankinen has had the hardest season of any goalie in the league by our numbers, and it's not close. He's 1-8 with an .805 save percentage, and he's allowed 15.2 more goals than his shots usually produce, last among 76 goalies in wins added. Over his last five starts he's 0-5, 9.3 goals worse than expected.

The breakdown is grim at both ends. He's stopped .545 of high-danger shots against a league .685, and .901 of low-danger shots against a league .963, so he's losing on the soft ones and the hard ones. Rebounds are an issue too. Vancouver gives up a lot, 3.79 expected goals per 60, but his numbers are far worse than even that defense explains.

This is also a second straight bad year: 20.3 goals worse than expected in 47 games last season, after he'd been well above average for Evolving-Hockey in 2024-25. Our talent range still expects him to recover toward .880, because save rates that low rarely last. He hasn't started since early November, and Leevi Merilainen won in Vegas on Sunday. His next start is the first test of whether he can win the net back.
